title: SPE Chapter 06 — Session
_comment: VET THIS FILE before rendering. lane 'app' = running page (optional 'js' Base API); lane 'code' = self-contained page from local source, lines hl highlighted. The flash toast is illustrated with Base.toast (the driver can't POST a form); it's the exact toast a real flash produces. Rebuild: RESYNTH=1 bash scripts/make-episode.sh 06-Session

scenes.narr: Chapter six adds the first thing a real site needs: state that survives between requests — sessions, and the messages that ride on them.
The session starts with hardened cookies: http-only, same-site, strict mode, and secure whenever the connection is encrypted.
On the first visit it mints a single random CSRF token and keeps it for the life of the session.
Every form that writes carries that token in a hidden field.
Rendered, of course, through the very same escaping helper as everything else.
And the server only accepts a write if the submitted token matches, compared in constant time. No valid token, no write.
So this contact form is a genuine, protected POST — the real form the server receives, first promised back in chapter two.
On a valid submission the model checks the input, queues a message, and redirects — the post-redirect-get pattern that stops a refresh from sending twice.
That redirect helper is typed to return never, and it exits, so nothing can run after it.
The queued message is a flash: written to the session, then read exactly once on the next page and immediately removed.
Each flash carries a level — success, warning, or danger — a backed enum that even maps itself to the right icon.
On the next page, Theme drains that queue and replays each message as a toast.

scenes.js: Base.toast('Thanks — your message is on its way.', 'success');
scenes.narr: Which looks like this: submit the form, and after the redirect your confirmation appears.
That is chapter six: sessions, CSRF-protected writes, and flash messages. Next, chapter seven gives the application a real database.
